headline: Last session: Sensex crashed 1,000 points as Indian benchmarks logged their longest weekly losing run in 25 years

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Monday, 5 October.

why: Foreign investors sold Indian stocks en-masse, wiping out Rs 9 lakh crore in a single session
Global rate hikes and rising oil prices triggered the worst monthly performance since March
The market failed to sustain gains amid high volatility and persistent selling pressure
Benchmark indices recorded an eight-week losing streak, a decline not seen in over two decades
whatHappening: The NSE and BSE are closed today for the weekend and were closed Friday for Gandhi Jayanti
D-Mart's Q2FY27 revenue grew 18.4% year-on-year to ₹19,206 crore
SEBI is reviewing position limits for non-agricultural contracts to improve market liquidity
FSSAI declared Nestle's Low Fat Dairy Whitener 'unsafe' following inspections in Delhi
summary: Indian markets are closed for the weekend after a sharp decline in the last trading session, which capped an eight-week losing streak. Foreign investor selling and global macro concerns wiped out significant investor wealth. Corporate news remains mixed, with D-Mart reporting strong revenue growth while Nestle India faces quality concerns.
